body_html:
How it works

The graph of a quadratic function is a parabola. If a > 0 it opens up (it has a minimum); if a < 0 it opens down (a maximum). The vertex is the turning point, and the axis of symmetry is the vertical line through it.

  • Standard form y = ax2 + bx + c: axis x = −b/2a; y-intercept (0, c).
  • Vertex form y = a(x − h)2 + k: vertex (h, k).
  • Factored form y = a(x − p)(x − q): zeros p and q; the axis is halfway between them.
Example

Find the vertex of y = x2 − 4x + 1.

x = −(−4) ÷ 2 = 2.

y = 4 − 8 + 1 = −3.

Answer: (2, −3)

Example

Describe y = −2(x + 1)2 + 3.

a = −2: opens down, narrower.

Vertex (−1, 3).

Answer: Maximum 3 at x = −1

Common mistakes

  • Sign errors in vertex form: (x + 3)2 means h = −3.
  • Using x = b/2a instead of −b/2a.
  • Reading the y-intercept as a zero.
  • Thinking a bigger |a| makes the parabola wider. It makes it narrower.

faq.q: How do you find the vertex of a parabola?
faq.a: In standard form, use x = −b/2a and substitute to find y. In vertex form y = a(x − h)² + k, the vertex is (h, k).

faq.q: What is the axis of symmetry?
faq.a: The vertical line through the vertex, x = −b/2a. The parabola is a mirror image on each side of it.

faq.q: How do you know if a parabola opens up or down?
faq.a: Look at a, the coefficient of x². If a is positive it opens up; if it is negative it opens down.

faq.q: How do you find the maximum height in a projectile problem?
faq.a: Find the vertex: the time is t = −b/2a, and the maximum height is the value of the function at that time.
